Rashi on Yevamot 36b:10:1.hebrew: אלא [משום] דרבנן - דמעוברת חברו מדרבנן היא, וקא מזלזלי בה, ומשום הכי קנסוהו דלא ליתי אחרינא למיעבד הכי:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:10:1.english: Only [due to] rabbinic [law] - For [the prohibition of] a woman pregnant [by] another man is rabbinic, and [people] treat it lightly, and therefore [the Sages] penalized him so that another [person] will not come to do so.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:10:2.hebrew: אבל הכא - יבמה מעוברת דאורייתא היא, ובדילי מינה, ולא בעי למיקנסיה להאי אטו אחריני:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:10:2.english: However, here - A pregnant yevamah is [a] Torah [prohibition], and [people] distance themselves from it, so there is no need to penalize this one on account of others.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:11:1.hebrew: ולדברי חכמים - דאמרי לכשיגיע זמנו לכנוס, יכנוס; מיהו עד שיגיע הזמן יוציא בגט, ולא סגי ליה בהפרשה בעלמא:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:11:1.english: And according to the statement of the Sages - Who say [that] when his time to marry [her] arrives, he may marry [her]; however, until the time arrives, he must send [her] out with a bill of divorce, and mere separation is not sufficient for him.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:11:2.english: As it teaches: "He must send [her] out" - "And the Sages say: He must send [her] out."

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:12:1.english: There we learned, etc. - Because he wants to ask: What [is the law] here?

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:12:2.english: Any [baby] that survived thirty days - From when it was born, it lived thirty days.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:12:3.hebrew: באדם אין נפל - להכי נקט באדם, דתני סיפא ובבהמה ח' ימים:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:12:3.english: In a human [it is] not a stillbirth - For this [reason it] specified "in a human," because the latter clause teaches, "And in an animal, eight days."

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:12:4.english: It is not a stillbirth - And [it] exempts its mother from chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:12:5.hebrew: ספיקא הוא - וחולצת ולא מתייבמת. ודוקא אי מספקא לן אי כלו לו חדשיו אי לא, אבל אי קים לן דכלו לו חדשיו, תנן במסכת נדה (דף מג:): תינוק בן יומו פוטר מן הייבום:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:12:5.english: It is a matter of uncertainty - and [the mother] performs chalitzah and does not enter into levirate marriage. And [this applies] specifically if we are uncertain whether his [gestational] months were completed or not; however, if it is established for us that his [gestational] months were completed, we learned in a Mishnah in tractate Niddah (43b): A one-day-old infant exempts [his mother] from levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:13:1.hebrew: מת בתוך שלשים - בן היבמה, ונתקדשה לשוק בחזקת שפטורה משום בנה:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:13:1.english: Died within thirty [days] - [This refers to] the yevamah's son, and she became betrothed to an outsider on the assumption that she was exempt on account of her son.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:14:1.hebrew: אם אשת ישראל היא - אם זה שקדשה ישראל הוא, שאם תחלוץ מן היבם לאחר קדושין לא תיאסר על בעלה, חולצת:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:14:1.english: If she is the wife of an Israelite - If the one who betrothed her is an Israelite, such that if she performs chalitzah with the yavam after betrothal she will not become forbidden to her husband, she performs chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:14:2.hebrew: ואם זה שקדשה כהן הוא - שאם תחלוץ תיאסר עליו, אינה חולצת, וסמכינן אולד:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:14:2.english: And if this [man] who betrothed her is a priest - For if she performs ḥalitza, she will become forbidden to him; she does not perform ḥalitza, and we rely on the offspring [having been viable].

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:1:1.hebrew: לעולם לא קנה כו' - לא אמתניתין פליג, אלא התם ביש נוחלין פליגי אמוראי בדיוקא דמתני', דכי אתא רבין אמר: ירש פלוני שדה פלוני ותנתן שדה פלוני לפלוני — רבי יוחנן אמר: קנה אפילו האי דירושה, דמדאדכר לשון מתנה בהאי שטר צואה לחד מינייהו, כולהו נמי מתנה נינהו. ור"ל אמר: לעולם לא קנה ההוא דירושה, דאמרינן להאי הוה מתנה ולהאי ירושה, עד שיאמר כו', דתיקו לשון מתנה אתרוייהו:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:1:1.english: [He] never acquires, etc. - He does not disagree with [our] Mishnah; rather, there in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin, the Amoraim disagree over a precise inference from the Mishnah. For when Ravin came [from the Land of Israel], he said: [If one says,] "So-and-so shall inherit such-and-such a field, and such-and-such a field shall be given to so-and-so" — Rabbi Yochanan said: Even this [recipient] of inheritance acquires [it], for since he mentioned the language of "gift" in this deed of will for one of them, all of them are also [considered] a gift. And Reish Lakish said: That [recipient] of inheritance never acquires [it], for we say that for this one it was a gift and for that one an inheritance, "until he says, etc." — so that the language of "gift" applies to both of them.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:2:1.hebrew: לאחר מותו - שכתב מהיום ולאחר מיתה, ואין לאב בהן אלא אכילת פירות בחייו:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:2:1.english: After his death - [Meaning] that he wrote "from today and after death," and the father has nothing in them except the consumption of produce during his lifetime.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:2:2.hebrew: מכר האב מכורין - לאכול הלוקח פירות כל ימי חיי האב, שזכה בזכות שהיה לו לזה בהן:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:2:2.english: [If] the father sold [them], they are sold - [meaning] for the buyer to consume the produce all the days of the father's life, since [the buyer] acquired the right that this one [the father] had in them.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:3:1.hebrew: ומת הבן בחיי האב רבי יוחנן אמר לא קנה לוקח - אפילו לכשימות האב, דקנין פירות שהיה לו לאב בנכסים הללו כקנין הגוף דמי, ואין מכירת הבן מכירה. ומתניתין דקתני "אין ללוקח בהן כלום עד שימות האב", הא כשימות האב יש לו — התם דמית האב בחיי הבן, ונתקיימה המתנה, ומה מכר ראשון לשני? כל זכות שתבא לידו. אבל מת הבן, לא בא זכות לידו:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:3:1.english: And the son died during the father’s lifetime; Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The purchaser does not acquire - Even when the father [eventually] dies, because the ownership of the usufruct that the father had in these properties is considered like ownership of the principal, and [therefore] the son’s sale is not a [valid] sale. And [as for] the Mishnah that teaches, "The purchaser has nothing in them until the father dies," [implying that] when the father dies he does have [a right to them] — that [refers to a case] where the father died during the son’s lifetime, and the gift was fulfilled; and what did the first [party] sell to the second? Every right that would come into his hand. However, [where] the son died [first], no right came into his hand.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:6:1.hebrew: תנא משום ר"א כו' - ר' אליעזר פליג אסיפא דמתני', וקאי אאין הולד של קיימא יקיים, וקאמר איהו: אע"פ שאין הולד של קיימא, קנסינן ליה דיוציא בגט, משום דנכנס לספק איסור אשת אח, ואע"ג דהשתא איגלאי מילתא דייבום מעליא הואי. ומיהו, בגט בלא חליצה סגי:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:6:1.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Eliezer, etc. - Rabbi Eliezer disagrees with the latter clause of the Mishnah, and refers to "[If] the offspring is not viable, he may keep [her]"; and he says: Even though the offspring is not viable, we penalize him that he must send [her] out with a bill of divorce, because he entered into a [situation of] possible prohibition of a brother's wife, even though now it has been revealed that it was a valid levirate marriage. However, a bill of divorce without chalitzah suffices.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:7:1.hebrew: דבר אחד - דר"מ נמי קניס את הנושא מעוברת חברו ומינקת חברו לגרשה. אשה שמת בעלה והיא מעוברת או מניקה, אסורה להנשא עד עשרים וארבעה חדש, שכן תינוק יונק:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:7:1.english: The same thing - For Rabbi Meir also penalizes one who marries a woman pregnant [by] another or nursing [another's child], [requiring him] to divorce her. A woman whose husband died and she is pregnant or nursing is forbidden to marry until twenty-four months [have passed], for that is how long a child nurses.

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:8:1.hebrew: ולכשיגיע זמנו לכנוס - לסוף כ"ד חדש יכנוס:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:8:1.english: And when his time comes to marry [her] - At the end of twenty-four months, he may marry [her].

Rashi on Yevamot 36b:9:1.hebrew: באיסור אשת אח - כלומר, שהיקל להכנס לספק אשת אח שיש לו בנים, דדלמא הוי ולד של קיימא. הלכך, קנסינן ליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 36b:9:1.english: With the prohibition of a brother's wife - That is to say, he acted leniently by entering into [a situation of] a doubtful [prohibition of] a brother's wife [where the brother] has children, for perhaps [the offspring] will be a viable child; therefore, we penalize him.

Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:10:1.hebrew: חיזוק לדבריהם יותר משל תורה - וההיא דהזהב (ב"מ נה:) גבי חמשה חומשין, דלא עשו אלא כשל תורה — משום דלא איצטריך לחיזוק. והכא גבי איסורא הוא דקניס ר"מ, אבל גבי ממונא, כגון כתובה, לא עשו חיזוק אפי' כשל תורה, דקאמר ר"מ בפ' אע"פ (כתובות נו: ושם): "כל המתנה על מה שכתוב בתורה — תנאו בטל, הא בדרבנן — תנאו קיים". וקצת תימה: אי רבנן דהכא היינו ר' יהודה — הא סבירא ליה גבי כתובה דעשו חיזוק לדבריהם יותר משל תורה! וי"ל: דבמילתא דשכיחא עבדו חיזוק, אבל הכא מילתא דלא שכיחא היא שישא אדם מעוברת חברו ומינקת חברו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:10:1.english: Reinforcement for their pronouncements more than [those] of the Torah - And [as for] that [passage] in [the chapter] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 55b) regarding the five fifths, where they made [the rabbinic fifth] only like [that] of the Torah — [that is] because there was no need for reinforcement. And here, it is with regard to a prohibition that Rabbi Meir penalizes, whereas with regard to monetary matters, such as a ketubah, they did not make reinforcement even [equal] to [that] of the Torah, as Rabbi Meir says in the chapter Af Al Pi (Ketubot 56b and there): "Anyone who stipulates [contrary] to what is written in the Torah — his condition is void; [implying that] in [a matter of] rabbinic [law] — his condition stands." And it is somewhat astonishing: if the Rabbis here are Rabbi Yehudah — behold, he holds regarding a ketubah that they made reinforcement for their pronouncements more than [those] of the Torah! And one can answer: that in a common matter they made reinforcement, whereas here, it is an uncommon matter for a man to marry another's pregnant [wife] or another's nursing [wife].

Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:11:1.hebrew: ולא קתני יפריש - והא דתני בסוטה בפ' ארוסה (סוטה דף כד. ושם) גבי מעוברת חברו ומינקת חברו: "יכול הוא להפרישה ולהחזירה לאחר זמן" — לשון הפרשה משמע הכי ומשמע הכי, אבל "יוציא" לא משמע אלא בגט. א"נ: התם, שקינא לה ונסתרה, לא חיישינן שיבא עליה, כיון דאסירא ליה מדאורייתא, ולא בעיא גט. והר"ר יוסף מאורליינ"ש הורה מטעם זה באחד שקידש מינקת חברו, שלא להצריך גט אלא הפרשה בעלמא (אפילו לרבי מאיר), כיון דבלאו הכי אסורה ליה — דכלה בלא ברכה אסורה לבעלה כנדה; ודוקא בנשא הוא דאמר הכא דבעיא גיטא, אע"ג דבקדש תוך ג' וברח, אי לאו דערוקיה מסתייה היה צריך ליתן גט — במעוברת ומינקת חבירו לא החמירו. ואין נראה, דמאי חומרא דכלה בלא ברכה ממינקת חבירו? דתרוייהו מדרבנן. וקצת היה מדקדק ר"י מהא דתניא התם (כתובות דף ס.): "מינקת שמת בעלה הרי זו לא תארס ולא תנשא", ואם כשאירס צריך ליתן גט — לא איצטריך תו למימר "לא תנשא". ומיהו י"ס דגרסי: "לא תנשא ולא תארס", ואיכא למימר ד"זו אף זו" קתני. ואפילו גרסינן "לא תארס ולא תנשא", מצי למימר דנקט "ולא תנשא" משום רבי יהודה, דאפילו לינשא שרי בתר י"ח חדש. ובשאלתות דרבי אחאי בפרשה וירא (סימן יג) כתוב גבי מעוברת ומינקת חברו, דהיכא דעבר וקדיש — מפקיע לה בגט מיניה, ואפילו אי הוה כהן מפסדינן לה מיניה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:11:1.english: And [they] do not teach: "He must separate" - And [as for] that which is taught in Sotah, in the chapter [entitled] Arusah (Sotah 24a and elsewhere), regarding another man's pregnant [wife] and another man's nursing [wife]: "He may separate from her and take her back after a period of time" — the term "separation" (hafrashah) implies either this [with a bill of divorce] or that [merely living apart], whereas "he must send out" (yotzi) implies nothing other than with a bill of divorce. Alternatively: there [in Sotah], where he warned her [against seclusion] and she secluded herself, we are not concerned that he will have intercourse with her, since she is forbidden to him by Torah law, and she does not require a bill of divorce. And Rabbi Yosef of Orléans ruled, based on this reason, regarding one who betrothed another man's nursing [wife], not to require a bill of divorce, but rather mere separation (even according to Rabbi Meir), since in any case she is forbidden to him — for a bride without a blessing is forbidden to her husband like a niddah; and it is specifically where he married [her] that [the Gemara] says here that she requires a bill of divorce, even though regarding one who betrothed within three [months] and fled, were it not that his flight suffices for him, he would have had to give a bill of divorce — regarding another man's pregnant or nursing [wife], they were not [so] stringent. But this does not seem [correct], for what stringency does a bride without a blessing have over another man's nursing [wife]? For both are rabbinic [prohibitions]. And Rabbi Yitzchak used to infer somewhat from that which is taught there (Ketubot 60a): "A nursing woman whose husband died — she may neither become betrothed nor marry," and if when he betrothed [her] he must give a bill of divorce, it would not need to state further "nor marry." However, there are texts that read: "she may neither marry nor become betrothed," and one can say that it teaches [in the style of] "not only this, but even that." And even if we read "she may neither become betrothed nor marry," one can say that it mentioned "nor marry" on account of Rabbi Yehudah, who permits [her] even to marry after eighteen months. And in the She'iltot of Rabbi Achai, in Parashat Vayera (Siman 13), it is written regarding another man's pregnant or nursing [wife] that where he transgressed and betrothed [her] — he releases her from himself with a bill of divorce, and even if he is a priest, we cause him to lose her [permanently]:

Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:12:1.hebrew: הא לא שהא ספיקא הויא - לא כמו שפי' הקונטרס דבפיהק ומת ולד איירי, דבהא אפילו רבנן מודו בפיהק ומת דנפל הוא; אלא כשנפל מן הגג או אכלו ארי איירי, כדאמר בס"פ ר' אליעזר דמילה (שבת דף קלו. ושם), והתם פסקינן כרשב"ג. וא"ת: ואמאי לא אזלינן בתר רוב נשים דולד מעליא ילדן? ואר"י: דחיישינן למיעוט מצוי כזה, כמו במים שאין להם סוף (לקמן יבמות קכא.) דאשתו אסורה, וגוסס שאין מעידים עליו להשיא אשתו; אע"ג דשמא התם משום ערוה החמירו, מ"מ כיון דמיעוט של נפלים מצוי — מחמירים ביה. ומחמירים נמי שלא לאכול בהמה תוך ח' ימים, כדאמרינן בס"פ ר' אליעזר דמילה (ג"ז שם). ומיהו לענין אבילות לא החמירו, שיש להקל באבלות, כדאמר בפ' יש בכור (בכורות מט.): "הכל מודים לענין אבלות שאין מתאבלים, דאמר שמואל: הלכה כדברי המיקל באבל". והא דתנן במסכת שמחות: "הספקות אוננים ומתאבלים עליהם", נראה דבספק בן ט' לראשון או ז' לאחרון איירי, דגנאי הדבר שלא יתאבלו לא זה ולא זה מאחר שודאי קרוב לאחד:
Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:12:1.english: "Were it not to survive, there would be uncertainty" - Not as Rashi explained, that it is speaking of where a child gasped and died, for in that [case] even the Rabbis agree that where it gasped and died it is [definitely] a stillbirth; rather, it is speaking of where it fell from the roof or a lion ate it, as it states at the end of the chapter Rabbi Eliezer deMilah (Shabbat 136a and there), and there we rule in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. And if you ask: Why do we not follow the majority of women, who give birth to viable children? Rabbi Yitzchak answered: Because we are concerned for a common minority such as this, just as in [the case of] water that has no visible end (below, Yevamot 121a), where his wife is forbidden [to remarry], and [the case of] a dying man, concerning whom we do not testify [that he is dead] to permit his wife to marry; even though perhaps there they were stringent because of [the severity of] forbidden sexual relations, nevertheless, since a minority of stillbirths is common, we are stringent regarding it. And we are also stringent not to eat an animal within eight days [of its birth], as we say at the end of the chapter Rabbi Eliezer deMilah (ibid.). However, with regard to mourning they were not stringent, as one is lenient in [matters of] mourning, as it says in the chapter Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 49a): "All agree with regard to mourning that they do not mourn, for Shmuel said: The law follows the one who is lenient in [matters of] mourning." And [as for] that which we learned in Tractate Semachot: "For uncertain cases, they observe aninut and mourn for them" — it appears that it is speaking of a case of uncertainty [whether the child is] a nine-month [child] of the first [husband] or a seven-month [child] of the second [husband], for it is unseemly that neither this one nor that one should mourn, since it is certainly a relative of one [of them].

Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:13:1.hebrew: מת בתוך שלשים יום כו' - נראה דהכי גרסי', ולא כרש"י דגריס בפ' ר"א דמילה (שבת קלו. ושם) "מת בסוף שלשים יום"; כיון דבפרק יש בכור (בכורות מט. ושם) אמרינן דיום ל' כשלפניו, מה לי ביום שלשים, מה לי תוך שלשים? ולמה ליה למינקט "ביום שלשים" טפי? ומיהו בה"ג כתב דביום שלשים אפי' פיהק ומת לרבנן לא הוי נפל, דדוקא תוך שלשים הוא דאמר בשבת (ג"ז שם) "פיהק ומת לד"ה מת הוא"; משמע דגרסינן הכא "מת ביום שלשים", דאי לאו הכי מנין היה להם חילוק זה? ועוד יש מקיים גירסא זאת אפילו בנפל מן הגג או אכלו ארי, וביום שלשים דוקא סמכי ארבנן. ושמא לענין אבילות נמי חשיב בר קיימא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:13:1.english: Died within thirty days, etc. - It seems that this is the correct reading [i.e., "within thirty days"], and not like Rashi, who reads in Chapter Rabbi Eliezer deMilah (Shabbat 136a, and there): "[If it] died at the end of thirty days"; for since in Chapter Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 49a, and there) we say that the thirtieth day is like [the days] before it, what is the difference [whether it says] "on the thirtieth day" or "within thirty days"? And why would [the Gemara] specifically state "on the thirtieth day"? However, the Ba'al Halakhot Gedolot wrote that on the thirtieth day, even if [the infant] gasped and died, according to the Rabbis it is not [considered] a non-viable infant, for it is specifically within thirty days that [the Gemara] states in Shabbat (ibid.): "If it gasped and died, according to all opinions it is [considered] dead [i.e., non-viable]"; this implies that we read here "[If it] died on the thirtieth day," for if not so, from where would they have this distinction? And furthermore, there is [an opinion that] upholds this reading even in a case where [the child] fell from the roof or was eaten by a lion, and [holds that] specifically on the thirtieth day do we rely on the Rabbis. And perhaps with respect to mourning as well, it is considered a viable child.

Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:1:1.hebrew: ואמר ריש לקיש לעולם לא קנה כו' - אע"ג דרבא גופיה קאמר ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קל.) דהלכה כרבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, מ"מ נפקא מינה דהלכה כר"ל לענין אחר שאין ראוי ליורשו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:1:1.english: And Reish Lakish said: He never acquires, etc. - Even though Rava himself says in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 130a) that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan ben Berokah, nevertheless there is a practical difference [in ruling] that the halakha is in accordance with Reish Lakish regarding another [person] who is not fit to inherit him.

Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:3:1.hebrew: ורבי יוחנן אמר לא קנה לוקח - וא"ת: לרבי יוחנן, אפי' לא מת הבן בחיי האב נמי לא ליקני, דהוי כמו (ב"מ טז.) "מה שאירש מאבא מכור לך", כיון דאלים קנין פירות כקנין הגוף? וי"ל: דלגבי הכי לא אלים קנין פירות לבטל לגמרי קנין הגוף דבן; וכיון דלבסוף אתיא שדה לידי דבן, חשיב מכר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:3:1.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The purchaser does not acquire [anything] - And if you ask: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, even if the son did not die during the father's lifetime, [the purchaser] should also not acquire [the field], for it is like (Bava Metzia 16a) "What I will inherit from my father is sold to you," since ownership of the produce is as strong as ownership of the land itself? And one can answer: With respect to this, ownership of the produce is not strong enough to completely nullify the son's ownership of the land itself; and since in the end the field comes into the son's hands, it is considered a [valid] sale.

Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:4:1.hebrew: קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי - מה שהתקינו באושא דאשה שמכרה בנכסי מלוג בחיי בעלה ומתה דהבעל מוציא מיד הלקוחות, לרבי יוחנן לא איצטריך. וכן משמע בהחובל (ב"ק דף פח: ושם), דמסיק תקנת אושא לר"ל. א"נ: קנין הגוף דאשה עדיף, שאין לבעל פירות אלא מכחה; ועוד, דאין לבעל פירות אלא בתקנתא דרבנן. וה"ר יעקב דאורליינ"ש תירץ, דאיצטריך תקנתא דאושא להיכא דכתב לה "דין ודברים אין לי בפירות נכסייך":
Tosafot on Yevamot 36b:4:1.english: Ownership of produce is tantamount to ownership of the principal - That which they enacted in Usha — that [if] a woman sold [some of her] melog property during her husband's lifetime and died, the husband recovers [it] from the purchasers — is not necessary according to Rabbi Yoḥanan. And so it is implied in [the chapter] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 88b and elsewhere), where [the Gemara] concludes [that] the enactment of Usha is according to Reish Lakish. Alternatively, the woman's ownership of the principal is stronger, for the husband has [rights to] the produce only by her power; and furthermore, the husband has [rights to] the produce only by rabbinic enactment. And Rabbi Yaakov of Orléans answered that the enactment of Usha is necessary for a case where he wrote to her, "I have no claim or rights in the produce of your property."
